editorial:
Imagine being the big star on your college football team, thinking you own the world, only to realize the real world does not care about your sports trophies. That is exactly what happens to our main guy in this 1929 flick. He heads to Wall Street to sell stocks, but he is honestly terrible at the business side of things. Luckily, he has a silver tongue and knows how to flirt. His boss notices this and gives him a sneaky job: use your charm to trick gullible women into buying stocks that are basically worthless. It is a funny setup that pokes fun at ego and greed in a lighthearted way.

Since the actual film footage is lost and we only have the audio, you have to use your imagination, which makes it a unique experience. The music and the dialogue carry the story, and the irony of the plot keeps things moving quickly. You will love the twist when he accidentally starts flirting with his own boss's wife. If you can find a high-quality audio restoration, it is a great piece of history. I suggest adding the digital archive copy to your collection or streaming it through a classic film library if you can find it.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when the main character's scheme backfires in the best way possible. After spending his time trying to trick women into buying bad stocks, he falls for the boss's wife. The tension peaks when the boss finds out his employee has been playing him. In the end, the football star learns a lesson about honesty and humility, moving away from his arrogant ways to find a more genuine path in life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school comedies and stories about arrogant characters getting humbled.
